title: Castlevania: Belmont’s Curse Relics Guide
summary:
The Castlevania series is no stranger to introducing game-breaking relics. Who could forget the Duplicator from Symphony of the Night, which let you reuse Library Cards to warp to the librarian's shop, throw infinite Buffalo Stars to destroy the toughest bosses, and chug endless healing potions, as long as it was equipped? In the same game, the Ring of Varda's stat buffs alone made every fight trivial.

Other Castlevania adventures also had their fair share of items that exploited that game's individual mechanics, so a dedicated Relics menu opens up plenty of possibilities. With over 40 options available, perhaps we'll see a combination of stuff that breaks this metroidvania wide open. In any case, you can only equip three at a time, so here are the best Castlevania: Belmont's Curse Relic combos and all of their locations.

How many relics are there in Castlevania: Belmont's Curse?

There are 44 individual relics in Castlevania: Belmont's Curse. You can equip up to three at once, each granting a tangible perk to Rose's combat abilities and spells.

The best Castlevania: Belmont's Curse Relic combos

Stacking damage-dealing relics to trigger after certain conditions are met is key to maximizing efficiency. However, we recommend you have a trio of other relics in mind to swap to whenever taking on boss fights.

For regular traversal, the combination of Obsidian Fang and Necro Charm can help massively with larger groups of foes. For example, if you go up against one of the lance knights and parry their attacks, they will become stunned, making for an easy kill. After killing them, you can do more damage to a nearby cluster of enemies.

Bosses require you to study their patterns to determine the relics best suited for the job. If you find yourself stabbing them in the back, the Vile Trinket rewards you with 25% bonus damage per hit. Tougher fights may need the Shadow Veil to buff Rose's defense at low health, while brawls against bosses that make you use lots of spells could benefit from the Twilight Gem to increase the damage each incantation costs you. Later on, the combination of Witch's Knot, Witch's Brew, and Haunting Relic is just too powerful to ignore.

We also recommend first-timers use the Crypt Key relic, as it restores all your health and mana whenever you open a chest. This is particularly handy if you want to go after the more dangerous relics and hidden weapons that you can find in locations, such as the perilous Clock Tower.

title: Next-Gen Xbox Could Be $1,800 And Launch In 2028 – Report
summary:
A new report sheds more details on Microsoft's plans for new Xbox hardware, including a new handheld device and console, and one of the biggest takeaways is the alleged price.

According to Fortune, the Project Helix console could cost between $1,200 and $1,800, unless Microsoft opts to subsidize the cost. The system could launch in 2028, the report said.

It's not uncommon for platform-holders to eat some of the cost of a new console and make up the difference with software and services. When the Xbox Series X and S platforms launched in 2020, then-Xbox CEO Phil Spencer said Microsoft was losing as much as $200 on every console it sold.

Part of what might be driving up the price for new consoles is the ongoing AI-fueled memory and component shortages. Microsoft itself is one of the biggest proponents of the build-out of all things AI, so its own efforts are contributing to an environment where the next Xbox could be incredibly expensive. Xbox CEO Asha Sharma reacted to this irony, saying it's "wonderful" that GPUs have use beyong gaming.

Richer households already made up the majority of console-buyers today, and that trend is expected to continue

Additionally, the report said Microsoft might release a "next-generation handheld device" for Xbox by the end of 2027, though there were no details on pricing or anything else.

Project Helix is the name for Microsoft's efforts for a "family of devices," so that would seemingly span both console and handheld.

The report added that Microsoft's Xbox and Windows teams reportedly battled over what software should run Project Helix, with the Windows team wanting the handheld to use a "trimmed-down" version of Windows Home. The Xbox team, meanwhile, reportedly pushed to build its own dedicated software.

An unnamed "senior Xbox executive" was said to have threatened to pull the plug on the entire handheld device rather than use Windows. Going forward, Xbox is "largely controlling the direction" of the handheld's OS, but Sharma told the site that the two teams work together. "We can't build Helix on our own," she said.

Sharma took over as Xbox CEO in February this year, immediately declaring that Xbox was in an unhealthy place and taking drastic measures that she believes may right the ship, including laying off staff, closing studios, and cancelling games. The layoffs, which have included about 2,000 people so far, are not done yet, as the Fortune story says more Xbox layoffs are coming this month, in November, and then again in January 2027.

Sharma also made major organizational changes, including handing Halo over to Activision for the future.

title: Watch Out GTA 6, A Shrek 2 Remaster Was Just Announced
summary:
A remaster of 2004's Shrek 2: The Game is on the way, according to an Xbox.com listing that was published too soon. Following the leak, Aspyr officially announced the Shrek 2 remaster, and it's releasing on November 10. That's just 9 days before GTA 6, so this November it's a battle of Shrek vs. GTA.

Shrek 2 Remastered is releasing November 10 for PS5, Xbox Series X|S, Switch 2, Switch, and PC, price at $30. People who prepurchase can get it for $27.

Like the original PS2, Xbox, and GameCube game, the remaster lets you play solo or in co-op with up to three friends, locally or online. The playable characters include Shrek, Fiona, and Donkey, among others.

In addition to the updated graphics, the Shrek 2 remaster includes a new Photo Mode and Cheat Mode. The original was published by Activision, but Aspyr Media is bringing this game to market. That company was also behind the recent The Lord of the Rings re-releases.

The official Shrek account recently posted a compilation of Shrek video game footage with the caption, "Only real gamers played Shrek," and many think it's connected to the Shrek 2 remaster. The compilation includes the OG Shrek 2 game, along with numerous others, including Shrek Smash N' Crash Racing and Shrek Super Party, the latter of which is one of Obsession star Inde Navarrette's favorite games.

It's already been a big year for Shrek in gaming, as Shrek recently came to Ubisoft's fighting game Brawlhalla and FIFA Heroes.

The original Shrek movie returned to theaters earlier this year to mark the franchise’s 25th anniversary. The long-awaited fifth movie, Shrek 5, is set for release in Summer 2027.

The Shrek movie franchise is a juggernaut, with its four main installments collectively grossing $3 billion, and that does not even count the Puss in the Boots spin-offs. In addition to Shrek 5, DreamWorks is producing a Donkey movie for 2028, with Eddie Murphy coming back to voice Donkey once again.

Beyond the movies, there are Shrek-themed attractions at Universal Studios theme parks, including the new kids-themed resort in Texas, while many fantastic Shrek memes have helped to keep Shrek popular and relevant for the past 25 years.

title: Here Are The Mechanics and Dozens Of New Cards From Magic: The Gathering’s Star Trek Set
summary:
After a year that featured alternate realities, ninja turtles, superheroes, and hobbits, the final Magic: The Gathering expansion of 2026 is going where no Universes Beyond set has gone before, as Star Trek is scheduled to launch in November.

Today, Wizards of the Coast revealed the mechanics players can expect in the set, along with dozens of new cards from both the main set and the preconstructed Commander decks. We also got a glimpse at some of the set's special treatments, including the seven cards that will come signed by the people depicted on the artwork.

Here's everything revealed during today's Magic: The Gathering Star Trek debut.

The mechanics of MTG Star Trek

Seven new mechanics--two of them found only in the Commander cards--highlight the set, along with a eighth mechanic returning from 2024's Edge of Eternities.

First is Beam Me Up, which allows you to cast certain spells from your graveyard by returning a creature you control to its owner's hand and paying a separate cost. The example card provided is Open Communications, which normally costs a single blue mana, but you can cast it again from your graveyard by returning a creature to its owner's hand and paying two generic and one blue mana.

Next is Face A Dilemma, which adds an additional wrinkle to a mechanic Magic fans are very familiar with. Basically, any time you have to choose a mode in a spell, you are "facing a dilemma," and there are cards in Star Trek that will give extra benefits simply because you made a choice. Seven of Nine, for example, lets you draw a card any time you have to make a choice on a modal spell.

Star Trek also introduces new modal spells, like the enchantment Kobayashi Maru Scenario. Every turn after casting this card, you must choose one of the four effects listed on the card, and you can't choose the same one twice--which means if you can't remove the enchantment after four turns, it's game over.

The next mechanic is Federation, which cares about the number of creature types among creatures you control that aren't the Borg (which makes sense, because the Federation and the Borg are like oil and water).

With Captain Jonathan Archer, by paying one green mana and tapping Archer, you can give another creature +X/+X until end of turn. As Archer is a Human Officer, and he creates a Dog token, that's at minimum +3/+3 on the first activation.

Starfleet Academy, meanwhile, allows you to pay five generic mana, tap it, and choose a color to add one mana of that color for every creature type among creatures you control. If you have a wide board of varied tokens, that could be a massive mana source.

Strange New Worlds is the next new mechanic, which cares about the lands you control. The more lands with different names you have on the board, the more effective these cards will be.

Deep Space Scan, for example, will let you draw a card for each differently named land on your side of the table. If you're playing a three-color deck, and you have an Island, a Mountain, and a Forest on the board, that's three cards coming to your hand.

Captain Pike, Fullness of Time, meanwhile, has his power and toughness determined by the number of differently named lands you control. If you're the type of person who likes to play different non-basic lands in your Commander deck, casting Captain Pike late in the game could result in a massive creature on the spot.

So far, we've focused on the good guy mechanics, now here's one for the baddies. Assimilate allows you to take any creature from a certain zone and add it to your battlefield, though it will become a Borg artifact creature instead of its other types.

Borg Cube lets you exile any creature on the board when it enters, and then when it attacks for the first time, you can add that exiled creature to your board as a Borg. Then, for every subsequent attack, you can repeat the process.

Borg Cube also shows off the major returning mechanic, Edge of Eternities' Spacecraft and Station mechanic. Multiple iconic spaceships from Star Trek's history appear on cards in the set, and they all have the Station mechanic, which allows a player to tap a creature in order to add charge counters to the Spacecraft equal to that creature's power. Once enough charge counters are added, the Spacecraft becomes an artifact creature and gains extra abilities.

For example, when three charge counters are added to D-7 Battle Cruiser, it will create a 2/1 Klingon Warrior creature token at the beginning of combat on your turn. When eight or more counters are added to it, it becomes a 3/3 flying creature.

The final two mechanics are exclusive to the Commander format, and only found on cards in the preconstructed commander decks. The first is Battlefront, which grants additional perks based on how many opponents you attack during a combat phase.

Worf, Defiant Commander is the face card of the Klingon Fury precon deck, and his Battlefront ability lets you exile a number of cards from the top of your library equal to the number of opponents you attacked. Until your next turn, you can play those cards as if they were in your hand.

Now, this ability only cares about players you actively attack. Abilities like myriad, which add tokens to the board already attacking, will not count toward a Battlefront ability, so choose wisely.

Seek Out is the other Commander-only mechanic, and it gives an added perk whenever you draw your second card in a turn, even if the permanent with the ability wasn't on the field when you drew your first card. Jean-Luc Picard, Luminary is the example card, as he gives a +1/+1 counter to a creature and two charge counters to a Spacecraft every time you draw your second card in a turn.

Booster Fun treatments

The Star Trek set will feature many themed treatments across its suite of products, and all of those were shown off during the stream as well.

First up are the seven Headliner Signature cards, which feature seven prominent faces from across Star Trek's history. Each of these cards will come with the authentic signature of the actor who portrayed the character; which means you could pull a Levar Burton, Patrick Stewart, Kate Mulgrew, or William Shatner autograph out of a Collector Booster pack, among others.

title: Xbox Series X|S Is Getting A Surprise Graphics Boost From AMD
summary:
Sony isn't the only company introducing new upscaling technology to its flagship PlayStation 5, as Microsoft and AMD have announced that FSR 4.1 is coming to more devices--including Xbox Series X|S consoles--in the future.

Similar to Sony's hardware-accelerated upscaling solutions for PS5 and PS5 Pro, AMD FidelityFX Super Resolution (FSR) 4.1 is an advanced, machine-learning-based temporal image upscaling and reconstruction technology that can render a game at a lower resolution and then upscale it to a higher resolution.

While it's highly doubtful that Xbox Series X|S consoles will start offering PS5 Pro-like graphics (both consoles lack dedicated hardware for machine-learning algorithms), this should still give owners a noticeable bump in graphical quality and performance if implemented properly.

"AMD has been an important partner in that journey for more than two decades. Van Vliet added that FSR 4.1 will come to Xbox Series X|S "soon," and that Microsoft and AMD are working to bring the tech to the next-gen Xbox console, Project Helix.

Beyond that, AMD didn't share any more details on FSR 4.1 for Xbox Series X|S. FSR 1 and FSR 2 relied primarily on spatial algorithms or basic temporal accumulation to upscale games, and questions remain about who will adopt the technology and add support.

Just because the latest version of FSR is out doesn't mean a game will automatically use it. For example, Capcom built the console versions of Pragmata around FSR 1, scaling up from 720p on Xbox Series S and 1080p on Xbox Series X. FSR integration requires manual developer work and testing, so results may vary. We're already seeing signs of this on PS5 with Quick Spectral Super Resolution; for now, only Marvel's Wolverine and Ghost of Yotei will support the new AI upscaling upgrade on base PS5 consoles.

Essentially, developers will have to actually patch their games to use it; AMD FSR 4.1 will not automatically upgrade every older game overnight. The announcement comes just weeks before the launch of Grand Theft Auto 6, and while Rockstar hasn't confirmed if its open-world game will utilize any upscaling technology like PSSR, QSSR, FSR 4.1, we could be looking at a current-gen arms race to find the best console to play the biggest game of the year on.

title: This Character-Action Zombie Game Stumbles Into Its Own Way
summary:
Stupid Never Dies makes a strong, if extremely weird, first impression. Wrapping roguelite progression around the system of an action-RPG and setting that story in an inventive punk-inspired world of monsters is an inviting hook. Plus, it's hard not to feel some affection for the dimwitted hero and his undoubtedly creepy quest to revive the supposed love of his afterlife. But the inventive world and a few neat ideas can only carry this game so far, and I ultimately struggled to look past the repetitive and often imprecise combat. 

The world of Stupid Never Dies has been completely taken over by monsters who emerged from inside the Earth's crust. These monsters are very conspicuously inspired by classic silver screen incarnations and popular B-movies, all filtered through a '90s or '00s pop-punk aesthetic. It's a stylish blend of influences that immediately identifies this game's goofball, self-effacing tone. 

When these monsters took over the world, they all but wiped out humanity. In the aftermath, a new caste system emerged, with zombies considered to be little more than cannon fodder in the fight for monster supremacy. Zombies who refused to fight in the war are seen as even lower than that--protagonist Davy is one of those, a teenage-looking undead who's more of a lover than a fighter.

In fact, Davy shambles his way into the adventure accidentally. He's just hungry, and happens to eat a weird glowing egg he finds laying around. This turns out to be a Phoenix Egg, giving him the ability to absorb power from other monsters. He doesn't really care to use this newfound power until an associate, Dr. Frank, tells him he may be able to use it to revive a dead girl named Julia who he's been infatuated with. Julia is a random human that Davy found in a freezer, and Davy sets his sights on reviving her solely because he imagines they would be a happy couple. 

This motivation doesn't give Julia any agency--we don't know whether she would even want to date a zombie, let alone Davy specifically, and that creates a problematic vibe for the setup. If the story treated this with any degree of seriousness it would be downright toxic. But this is not a serious game, and Davy is very pointedly presented as a complete dumbass, so I at least think we as the audience are supposed to recognize the obvious folly in his lovelorn puppy act. Still, it's a bit ick. 

This uncomfortable setup is also just quickly drowned out with lore and jokes. There's a ton of exposition at the very start to introduce you to this world, but a lot of it is delivered with a sort of "just go with it" haste. It seems at once proud of its stylish mash-up and embarrassed by it as a thin pretense for fighting movie monsters. The humor, similarly, is mostly kept just barely on the right side of cringe, though parts of the story occasionally veer over into being too cheesy or silly. 

To have any hope of reviving Julia, Davy has to defeat and absorb the power of KOM, the nickname given to the King of the Monsters. After destroying Earth, most of the monster races burrowed back underground, leaving only the lowly zombies to roam around on the surface. Davy descends into deeper and deeper layers to find new materials in his quest to revive Julia, all leading toward KOM. If he completes a particular boss target or takes a ride back to their home base in an abandoned shopping mall before being defeated, he keeps his gains and can cash them in for power-ups. That's where the roguelite structure comes in.

In the underground combat segments, Davy can move quickly and strike hard, behaving much like a hero in a character-action game. The enemies are nicely differentiated between mobs like lizardmen and skeletons and elites like cyclopes and harpies, offering a good bit of variety, especially since you can absorb the powers of elite enemies. (More on that momentarily). 

By default, Davy's moves feel floaty--flailing and imprecise. This makes sense, as he is a zombie, but it does mean your core moveset never feels very cool or stylish. Devil May Cry this game isn't. You can also parry enemy strikes--the game insists on exclusively calling this a "stupid parry" for no particular reason--or leap to reach flying enemies or knock them into walls or off the stage. Combat has a fun sense of chaos and momentum to it. 

As you level up, in roguelite fashion, you'll gain new perks to equip and upgrade. Some of these are fairly straightforward, like boosts to your attack or defense, while others are more specialized, like giving you a passive perk for how many enemies you've knocked off the edge of a stage. 

On top of that, Davy has a Bite ability, which you charge up through regular attacks. This functions as both a heal and a finisher, as you can chomp down on enemies to restore some Hit Points, but it's better saved to use as the fatal blow on an elite enemy, since that heals you for a greater amount and grants you a big power boost. A lot of the combat is about managing your bite gauge, building it up for a big enemy, and then chomping into an elite for an impactful heal.

Elite enemies also often drop skill cores that you can bite into as long as you have your gauge charged, which lets you add their transformation to a quick select. These are worth using instead of saving, since they expire, but they turn Davy into a super-powerful creature like a werewolf, lich, or snow fairy. Those greatly expand Davy's abilities and make him much more powerful than his standard zombie form. And like the regular upgrades, they also come in different rarities, so it's always exciting to see a legendary monster form that you know will really tear through enemy mobs or that impending boss. 

It all works pretty well, but progression can be achingly slow, and the early battles get repetitive fast. I found the game actually became much more fun in the "Go Nuts" mode, a modifier that makes your level progression much faster to speed you along, especially in the early stages. Stupid Never Dies hits its stride about halfway through each run, I found, so breezing past the early parts to get to the meat of the gameplay was just a better way to play. 

When you get back to base, there are a variety of upgrade systems. You have Bessie, who sells you upgrades you'll be able to find in the dungeons from then on; a nearby monster who gives you achievement rewards for completing milestones; Acelino, a weredog who can swap your body parts to build out Davy with various stat boosts and abilities; Milo's ice cream shop, which lets you trade giblet gelato for ranked skill and stat upgrades; and Julia, who you can give gifts to in order to earn stat upgrades to the Davy Burst, his super-powered ultimate state. In this base, you can also explore to talk with Dr. Frank about your monster dex, view and heart Julia's old social media posts, or change your soundtrack tunes.

The multitude of systems isn't exactly elegant, and what's worse, Davy always starts in the mall with a slow zombie shamble. You quickly unlock the ability to ride around on a motorized vacuum, but it's just baffling why you have to press the button to board the quicker ride every time. I can't imagine anyone ever wanting to actually walk around at his default slow pace, so why force the transition at all?

Other elements are similarly unwieldy. Bessie's upgrades are mostly understandable but sometimes the sheer number of variables just gets confusing, which at best breaks the momentum of a stage when you have to pause to decipher an ability, and at worst just gets so confusing that I'd bypass it altogether. On one recent run I had the option to choose an upgrade for: "Rate decrease for recoverable damage reduction over time +100." This was a good card judging by its rarity, but I honestly couldn't make heads or tails of what the heck it was supposed to do.

Then there's the addition of a timer, as indicated by a TickTock Teddy in the corner of your screen. This incentivizes you to skip some layers strategically since you simply do not have time to play all of them in a single run, and time-extension items give you one more thing to earn while you're choosing which layers to play. But it feels half-baked, since the difficulty of the bosses alone is enough of a friction point, and nothing feels as frustrating as nearly defeating a boss and then being brought down by an arbitrary time restriction. 

The time pressure also just makes certain aspects of the level design feel bad in unexpected ways. Airborne enemies are a particular pain because they are hard to hit and take longer to defeat, and you can just feel the timer counting down. Randomized stages can sometimes be difficult to navigate, wasting precious time. Even the long approach down a dark corridor to a formidable boss, which could feel properly dramatic and tension-building, instead just made me think of how much time I was burning on the way. 

These caveats and friction points ultimately harm the overall experience. The combat and merchant systems feel just a little too overstuffed and the timer is a frustrating and unnecessary addition that detracts from the overall flow of moving through the world. Stupid Never Dies has some good ideas going for it, including an inventive world, a likable idiot of a protagonist, and some cool combat mechanics like transforming into elite enemies. But it also has a lot of cringey plot points and jokes, repetitive and slow progression, and an awful timer system. I wish I could have enjoyed the positive aspects more, without the other cruft getting in the way.

title: Hideo Kojima Returns To Night City For Cyberpunk: Edgerunners Season 2
summary:
Cyberpunk: Edgerunners Season 2 officially launches tomorrow on Netflix, and while the show features a new cast, it also includes one familiar face: veteran game designer Hideo Kojima, who'll cameo as Hideyoshi Oshima in the series.

"He's a huge fan of Edgerunners and wrote a lot of nice things about it," showrunner Bartosz Sztybor said to GameSpot in a recent interview. "He also had a cameo in Cyberpunk 2077. Here in Edgerunners 2, it's the same character he played in Cyberpunk 2077, so that's the connection."

In Cyberpunk 2077, Oshima plays a braindance producer from Tokyo who wants to create BD experiences that are emotionally resonant with viewers, rather than the more salacious media that made the technology so popular. Modeled after and voiced by Kojima, Oshima pops up in the Konpeki Plaza during the "Heist" mission. Later in the game, players can also find a Bridge Baby Pod Easter egg, a reference to his game Death Stranding.

Beyond the cameo (and bit parts in Zootopia 2), Kojima is pretty busy right now. Death Stranding 2: On the Beach was released last year, and his next Xbox projects include a new take on horror in the form of OD and the action-espionage game Physint, which stars Bill Skarsgard as the protagonist.

Cyberpunk Edgerunners Season 2 premieres on Netflix starting on October 20, with a 10-episode block of Night City adventures featuring a quartet of new characters. A big-screen movie adaptation is also in development, while work continues on the Cyberpunk 2077 sequel, Cyberpunk 2.

title: CoD: Modern Warfare 4 Has Thrilling Campaign And Exciting DMZ Mode Changes
summary:
In 2019, Infinity Ward rebooted Call of Duty's Modern Warfare series, delivering a gritty and polished campaign featuring Captain Price and the assembly of the iconic Task Force 141. Despite the strong start, the series' sequels stumbled a bit, with  Modern Warfare 3 in particular standing out as having a weak story and open-world missions that missed the mark. But with Modern Warfare 4, Infinity Ward returns the series' campaign to strength with a satisfying narrative and well-crafted missions for an epic conclusion to the rebooted series.

Modern Warfare 4's single-player goes back to being a traditional and mostly linear experience that some recent entries have strayed from. There is only one open-world mission this year, and it is far more engaging than the previous attempts. Modern Warfare 4 doesn't introduce anything new or innovative, but it finds success with a consistently strong narrative and engaging gameplay built on nail-biting tension. Thankfully, you're never forced into any mission objectives that feel like silly chores or ill-timed distractions. Every mission in Modern Warfare 4 carries urgency and drives the plot forward.

That plot closes out the ongoing narrative surrounding Price and Task Force 141, but it also takes Call of Duty to Korea and introduces a fresh new cast of characters. The campaign intertwines two seemingly separate stories for an over-the-top, globetrotting affair across New York City, Paris, and Mumbai, in addition to several parts of Korea. This is the explosive Hollywood-style action you'd expect from a Call of Duty campaign at a quality level we haven't seen from the franchise in years--that includes the recent Black Ops entries.

One half of the game places you in the boots of Private Park, a young South Korean soldier, who has never experienced real combat before. Private Park and his squad are forced to fight back to save their country when North Korea launches an invasion.

The other half of the campaign follows the events of Modern Warfare 3 and the aftermath of John "Soap" MacTavish's death. In Modern Warfare 4, Captain Price is in a much darker place, going rogue to hunt down Makarov and also tie up any other loose ends with the villain's associates.

This new outlaw version of Price ties back to one of the most-telling quotes of Modern Warfare 2019, where he lays out his ethos on where the lines in war are."You draw the line wherever you need it, Sergeant," Price says. "End of the day, someone has to make the enemy scared of the dark. We get dirty and the world stays clean. That's the mission."

That line is seemingly in a place no one could have foreseen, as Price is furious and more willing than ever to get his hands dirty in pursuit of making everyone allied with Makarov scared of the dark. Being on the run leaves Price with very few allies, though. In a desperate attempt to reach the Archer (Mads Mikkelsen), who is another threat linked to Makarov, Price makes a deal with Valeria Garza and the cartel.

Price hasn't turned into a complete monster, but the cartel don't mind blasting through civilians in order to achieve their mission. This team-up makes for chaotic gunfights through Paris and engaging banter between the characters. Price is constantly trying to look out for civilians and wants to minimize the collateral damage, but Valeria just comically taunts him, calling him Papi and old man, as she operates with less strict rules. The extent to which Price is a contrast to Valeria becomes a key part of the story. After a chase scene where they commit a particularly brutal act of violence, Valeria tells Price that "he's still a good guy," but she is a notorious cartel leader trying to get paid for delivering a weapon to the bad guy, so how much weight can her words really carry?

Price's cartel team-up also leads him to realize this weapon delivery is dangerous enough to shift the balance of power, setting in motion a much greater conflict. To make matters worse, Price also has a target on his back as the remaining members of his Task Force 141 team, Simon "Ghost" Riley and Kyle "Gaz" Garrick, are sent to capture or kill him.

This manhunt for Price leads to a standout mission called Gone Dark, where your POV switches to Gaz as he hunts Price inside of a dark hotel. At the start of the series, Captain Price served as a mentor and moral compass for Gaz, so there's a lot of emotional weight to the mission as Gaz, and the player, see just how far Price has fallen from a clearer third-party perspective. There are shocking moments and intense exchanges between the now fractured members of Task Force 141 that leverage the squad's long history effectively. There's an emotional pull throughout the mission, as Price begs Ghost and Gaz to back off, and a bigger gut punch when Price says he doesn't want to kill them, but implies he will. These moments really nail down how Price's moral compass has broken. The events of Gone Dark also set up a powerful moment in a later mission to bring the series full circle in a way I appreciated.

The Korean invasion intertwines with Price's epic revenge tour, causing the new South Korean squad and US forces to team up. Although that may seem overwhelming, even with these shifting POVs and a non-chronological story, the narrative flows well from mission to mission, keeping things moving at a good clip through stealth missions, on-foot and vehicular chase sequences, slow-motion breach-and-clear segments, and even some satisfying action of manning a chopper gunner. There's also a Clean House-style mission with night-vision goggles, where you need to clear rooms with extreme trigger discipline to avoid shooting any civilians.

Building on the success of the DMZ beta launched in 2022, Infinity Ward elevates the extraction mode with major upgrades for Modern Warfare 4, including a more dynamic map, an engaging social hub, in-depth story missions, and deeper progression. All of this allows for more replayability and new ways to experience the sandbox magic that can happen within a match of DMZ. In fact, most of Infinity Ward's Call of Duty innovation this year is packed within DMZ, and thanks to a satisfying gameplay loop, the extraction mode is the standout part of Modern Warfare 4.

Matches of DMZ allow for up to 60 players to group up in trios. Each squad is tasked with surviving and extracting before a circle of irradiated gas floods the map, killing everyone in its path. This is PvPvE gameplay with a focus on exploration, combat, and a wide variety of missions. As with most extraction shooters, dying in DMZ means losing everything, making it a high-risk for high-reward game mode.

DMZ's new Hajin map is a vast upgrade from the original Al Mazrah location. This is the largest map ever created for Call of Duty, outsizing Warzone's Verdansk and even Black Ops 7's massive Avalon map, allowing for deeper exploration and greater map diversity. Hajin is set in a fictional version of the demilitarized zone between North and South Korea, and the area provides a wide range of main and secondary points-of-interest.

In the hours I spent playing DMZ, my squadmates and I always seemed to spawn in a new area. No match ever felt the same, and there was always so much more we wanted to explore before our time ran out. Al Mazrah's diversity of locations doesn't even come close to Hajin, which takes you through dense forests, as well as a selection of city-based locations, such as military compounds, underground tunnel systems, and even an irradiated nuclear power plant.

Updated NPC behavior and dynamic weather make Hajin feel more alive than Al Mazrah. Rain or fog can roll in at any time but aren't guaranteed in every match. Weather changes don't affect the entire map and are randomly localized to specific areas, shifting how you experience Hajin from point-to-point. Fog can be beneficial for stealth as it hinders the view of everyone in the vicinity, including NPC enemies, but it also limits your ability to check your surroundings. Rain on the ground (or traversing through other water sources) can create audible sloshy footsteps, betraying your position. I'm always skeptical about dynamic weather in games, but Modern Warfare 4's graphics are stunning, and it was impressive watching the fog roll across the coast and move inland. And on at least one occasion, driving through dense fog allowed my squad to evade an entire convoy of enemies. Fog is more impactful than the rain, but both are a welcome touch to the world, as they can change how you approach a situation, and they add a bit of immersion and variety to matches.

With Hajin, you'll see enemies moving through the world in a more organic way. At military bases, you might find soldiers doing push-ups outside in the yard, while patrol cars full of enemies drive around the map. Drones search the sky in various locations, suicide-bomber robo-dogs can chase you around, and a boss-level tank patrols the streets. The AI threats aren't smarter, but these behaviors and a wide range of enemy types provide a sense of immersion and make for engaging combat encounters. You also can't underestimate them entirely because of their lack of intelligence in combat, as they can easily overwhelm you with their numbers. In the higher-tier zones, the NPCs have heavier armor and some wield riot shields, so it takes firepower and strategy to take them down.

Changes to progression make the experience much more rewarding. You can load into a match with the intent of looting cash and resources, hunting other players, engaging in story missions, or completing smaller side objectives. No matter how you choose to play, all of these actions count toward your DMZ player level, and you earn this XP even if you fail to successfully extract. You'll also earn player XP and weapon XP for multiplayer and Warzone, but you can only rank up your DMZ level by playing DMZ.

Teammates are added to the FOB of whoever is hosting the party, so there is a social element as well, but this base is also a crucial command center that evolves with you as you level up in DMZ. This adds another layer to DMZ's engaging gameplay loop, as you're constantly trying to level up and unlock helpful stations and upgrades within your FOB, including a vendor, bounty board, dog tag case, and more importantly, a 3D printer for crafting crucial gear.

There are no Buy Stations on the map this year, meaning you can't purchase what you need during the match. This is a positive change that prevents everyone from getting their hands on powerful items right away. You'll have base weapons and gear to start, but you'll need to do some scavenging in your matches in order to get better equipped. This change puts more emphasis on looting and exploration, requiring you to search out guns and gear in-match, or at the very least, find the resources to craft what you need. DMZ also no longer lets you build custom weapons without paying to do so. Once you've reached level 10, you'll unlock the Gunsmith FOB station. The base price for guns isn't pricey, but you'll need to pay to unlock attachment slots as well as each individual attachment you want to include. Slots also get more expensive, so you can end up spending a lot to fully customize a single gun that you risk losing every time you load into a match. You can choose to load into a match with a free random loadout consisting of the most basic gun and supplies, but ultimately, the Gunsmith change adds more weight to your decision to risk something expensive or play it safe with less-effective gear.

You have the option to spend in-game money to send an evac team to rescue them from Hajin. This can get pricey if they are a high-level operator, but it's a relief to have the option to salvage something from your loss.

There are often several layers of complexity to extraction modes, so they can feel overwhelming and confusing at first. DMZ's menus and mission deployment options are no different in that regard, especially with all the new bells and whistles baked into the mode. Beyond that, DMZ offers various mission types to choose from, and it's initially difficult to differentiate what each type offers.

Hopefully this doesn't lead to players getting bigger advantages such as UAVs or high-rarity guns. In-game bonuses are best handed out as cosmetic items like operator and vehicle skins.

Once you get past the confusing mission lingo, DMZ settles into a sandbox experience with all the thrills of a high-risk/high-reward extraction shooter. Despite the original DMZ being an engaging concept, it struggled with barebones features and weak missions, but you can see how it served as the building blocks for Modern Warfare 4's more robust and engaging gameplay loop. Much of the magic often comes from the chaos that builds as you fight or flee through dangerous areas of Hajin, and the new progression layers make it easy to get lost in the world of DMZ. Overall, Infinity Ward has elevated Call of Duty's extraction mode with engaging features and riveting gameplay, and I can't wait to jump into my next match on Hajin.

The base price for guns isn't pricey, but you'll need to pay to unlock attachment slots as well as each individual attachment you want to include. Slots also get more expensive, so you can end up spending a lot to fully customize a single gun that you risk losing every time you load into a match. You can choose to load into a match with a free random loadout consisting of the most basic gun and supplies, but ultimately, the Gunsmith change adds more weight to your decision to risk something expensive or play it safe with less-effective gear.

Leveling operators in the beta was simplistic, but MW4 gives you three different trait trees you can invest in: Warfighter, Scout, and Survivalist. The longer an operator stays alive, the more powerful they become and the more upgrades they can acquire, but dying in Hajin means you've lost that specific operator inside the DMZ zone. This sounds devastating if you've invested time into leveling up an operator and upgrading their traits, but they're not permanently lost. You have the option to spend in-game money to send an evac team to rescue them from Hajin. This can get pricey if they are a high-level operator, but it's a relief to have the option to salvage something from your loss.

There are often several layers of complexity to extraction modes, so they can feel overwhelming and confusing at first. DMZ's menus and mission deployment options are no different in that regard, especially with all the new bells and whistles baked into the mode. You are onboarded with a brief tutorial mission to teach you the ropes, but this mostly teaches you how to follow mission markers and heal yourself after a fight. Beyond that, DMZ offers various mission types to choose from, and it's initially difficult to differentiate what each type offers.

There are currently only six main story missions available, but they are engaging multi-step story objectives. One mission sent us on a fun casino heist, where we had to locate and breach a vault, hijacking as many bags of cash as we could before irradiated gas spread through the vault. Another tasked my squad with locating a hostage in a hospital, who was handcuffed to a gurney, and we had to wheel them out to an exfil location while enemy forces made our exit difficult. I wish there were more than six missions, but they were a blast to play, and you can opt for different strategies to complete them. 

The charm of DMZ remains the random and chaotic moments you get with the sandbox nature of the mode, and the living world of Hajin definitely elevates the unpredictability, allowing every playthrough to feel unique. The world is also filled with smaller missions and objectives, so there are still many ways to play and level up.

DMZ addresses the elephant in the room, which is the growing divide between players in extraction shooters. Some players believe the games should always have a PvP focus while others want the extraction experience in a PvE environment. DMZ attempts to appeal to both sides with its approach to PvP. Killing players now activates a heat level, which is similar to the Wanted system in GTA, and you'll earn a marked bounty on your head. The more players you kill, the higher your Wanted bounty grows. Hajin has bounty board stations, where it shows all active players in the match who are marked as Wanted. This bounty board lets you either pay cash to reduce your own heat level, or you can buy intel to locate the other Wanted players. This feels like a great way to cater to the PvP-focused extraction players, allowing them to hunt each other down for large sums of money, while passive players can stay off the radar if they avoid killing other operators.

Another major change this year is that DMZ is no longer a free-to-play mode tied to Warzone, and instead is packed into Modern Warfare 4 as part of its $70 price tag. While losing a free game is always a bummer, the amount of upgrades packed into DMZ do feel worthy of a premium buy-in.

While it's not pay-to-win per se, DMZ does provide additional benefits to players who purchase the pricey Vault edition of Modern Warfare 4. This gives them access to an additional operator slot, two medium-size backpacks, two armor-plate carriers, and other beneficial but single-useitems. Vault edition owners getting these freebies isn't a major concern, as the specific items don't have a huge impact on whether or not you lose a fight against them. However, this gets tackier when the game stops being free-to-play, and there's always the worry it's a downhill slide toward further bonuses that do become pay-to-win. Hopefully this doesn't lead to players getting bigger advantages such as UAVs or high-rarity guns. In-game bonuses are best handed out as cosmetic items like operator and vehicle skins.

Once you get past the confusing mission lingo, DMZ settles into a sandbox experience with all the thrills of a high-risk/high-reward extraction shooter. Despite the original DMZ being an engaging concept, it struggled with barebones features and weak missions, but you can see how it served as the building blocks for Modern Warfare 4's more robust and engaging gameplay loop. Much of the magic often comes from the chaos that builds as you fight or flee through dangerous areas of Hajin, and the new progression layers make it easy to get lost in the world of DMZ. Overall, Infinity Ward has elevated Call of Duty's extraction mode with engaging features and riveting gameplay, and I can't wait to jump into my next match on Hajin.

title: Sony Boss: “Creativity Is For Humans, Not AI”
summary:
Take-Two boss Strauss Zelnick and Sony Group President and CEO, Hiroki Totoki, commented on the future of gaming today at the Paley International Summit. Naturally, the topic of AI came up, and Totoki believes AI technologies will not replace humans in game development, in part because of the creativity required.

"Creativity is for humans, not AI,” Totoki said, as reported by IGN. “How to use the technology profile is important. Of course, I encourage my people to use AI in a certain manner, but at [the] same time we try to keep the rights and rights holders and creators and artists.”

For his part, Zelnick said it's his belief that AI itself will not replace a developer, but instead, people who don't embrace AI might be replaced by people who do.

"I’m fond of saying AI is a collection of datasets, compute, and large language models. That’s what it is. And datasets, by definition, are backward-looking. That’s all they are. And creativity, at its best, is forward-looking," he said.

Zelnick said ideas that are "completely unexpected" don't come from algorithms--they come from creative people making surprising, original choices. To make his point, Zelnick said when he was an executive at Fox, he oversaw the release of Home Alone, a movie that no one expected to be a success.

"It turned out to be the highest-grossing comedy of all time. So if hits are unexpected, data sets aren’t gonna get you there, no matter how fluent they are," he said.

Both PlayStation and Take-Two have embraced AI, with PlayStation heavily leveraging the technology in its game-development processes. As for Take-Two, the publisher is utilizing the technology for its workflows, but there is no AI in GTA 6.

There has been significant pushback for AI in game development from developers and players alike, with many expressing concerns about job security, legal issues, and simply the further "enshi**ification" of everything they love.

title: 10 Years After The Switch 1 Reveal, I Still Haven’t Played A Game At A Rooftop Party
summary:
It's now been a full decade since Nintendo announced the first Switch, which is almost hard to believe, given how fresh that reveal trailer still feels in our heads. Heaps of hype and a lack of information from Nintendo about its Wii U successor, codenamed "NX," led to the company's fanbase becoming increasingly restless.

Reports and rumors pointed to the NX as a console-handheld hybrid, but Nintendo didn't fully unveil the Switch until October 20, 2016 (an announcement preluded by a photo of Mario being a creep). The three-and-a-half-minute video made it clear how Nintendo wanted players to interact with the Switch, showing several scenarios where people take their games on the go.

Rewatching that trailer today, it's amusing to look back at how Nintendo foresaw the social impact of the Switch. Some moments from the trailer manifested in reality, while others were hilariously exaggerated.

You have a guy taking his dog (and his copy of The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild) out on a walk, a traveler playing Skyrim on a plane and putting the game on his television upon his arrival home, and professional Splatoon players practicing before their big moment on stage.

And then, there's "Nintendo Karen." The most-talked-about moment in the trailer centered on a woman playing Super Mario Odyssey before being prompted to join friends for a rooftop party (a typical gathering of millennials, as people would joke back then), during which she breaks out the Switch, pulls out that dinky little kickstand, and plays a game with a friend as onlookers holding red Solo cups watch with indifference. Fans branded this commercial character as "Karen" and debated the social implications of bringing a Switch to such a function.

The Nintendo Switch reveal trailer remains a striking piece of marketing, with its upbeat vibe and extra emphasis on the Switch's branding (much needed, after the Wii U's marketing failures). In the years since the Switch's release, I’ve seen Switches out in the wild, just as Nintendo imagined, though I've yet to go to a rooftop party like the one Karen attended.

While the Switch 2 continues to sell well, there's a notion that its reveal was a bit cold and lacking in fanfare compared to the original Switch. Even so, Nintendo still hasn't lost its charm and quirk, even though the company will probably never use that hilarious picture of Mario behind the curtain ever again.

title: Xbox Game Pass’s Newest Wave Is Headlined By A Huge Final Fantasy Adventure
summary:
Right on schedule, the second wave of games coming to Xbox Game Pass has been revealed. After the first batch, which included Gears of War: E-Day, Battlefield 6, and more, the rest of the month will add games like Final Fantasy 7 Remake and The Seance of Blake Manor to the subscription service. We've also gotten a sneak peek at what's coming in November, so there's plenty to play over the next couple of weeks.

As a reminder, several games are also leaving Xbox Game Pass this month, including a pair of Double Fine classics and one massive Star Wars Lego game.

Final Fantasy 7 Remake Intergrade is the headline act in this new wave of arrivals, right on time for anyone looking to experience the saga from its first chapter. The Intergrade version includes the original game and its Yuffie-centric expansion, but you'll have to wait until October 29 to embark on the Unknown Journey.

Before then, you can grab the Game Preview edition of Sandustry on PC starting October 21. A game about exploration and automation, it's a tempting download for anyone who enjoys assembly-line video games. You can also get Dodo Duckie on October 22, a reality-bending odyssey where you'll get to outsmart aliens and solve puzzles while wielding duck powers, and October 26 will see the MMO-lite action RPG Scramble Knights Online make its day-one debut on Game Pass.

The Séance of Blake Manor was one of GameSpot's favorite games of 2025, and you can check out this supernatural detective mystery for yourself when it's added to the Game Pass library on October 27. Starting October 29, you can explore Midgar in the aforementioned Final Fantasy 7 Remake Intergrade, play classic Plants vs. Zombies in HD, and the horror-parkour game Terrible Lizards is another day-one release to round out the month.

Looking ahead, November will kick off with Pit of Goblin, an online horror co-op adventure in which you play as a scrappy goblin.

title: Here’s An Exclusive Look At How Cyberpunk: Edgerunners’ Cast Will Look In The Hit Trading Card Game
summary:
Earlier this year, a new trading card game based on the hit Cyberpunk franchise hit Kickstarter and became the highest-funded game in Kickstarter's entire history. With the launch set now out in the wild, WeirdCo is ready to announce the game's first expansion, Edgerunners: Burn Bright, which is scheduled to launch in Spring 2027.

Edgerunners: Burn Bright will introduce multiple characters, locations, and moments from the popular Netflix anime into the card game, along with new mechanics which will be revealed closer to the set's release date. The set will also introduce a new chase rarity, though WeirdCo did not share further details.

We have an exclusive reveal of the artwork for one of the characters joining the Cyberpunk TCG through the Edgerunners: Burn Bright set, as well as his trusty firearm. Here's the artwork for Zhou, Maine's Answer!

Zhou, or the L-69 Zhuo, is the two-handed shotgun wielded by Maine, the leader of the crew David Martinez joins in the first season of Edgerunners. While we don't know what Zhou's abilities are yet, we expect it will be a powerful Gear card that will enhance whoever it's equipped to. Perhaps it will even give an additional bonus to Maine himself, but we won't know for sure until we see what the card can do..

The Cyberpunk TCG's second expansion, Edgerunners: Burn Bright, launches Spring 2027 in both local game stores and big-box retailers.

title: Netflix’s Push Into Gaming Continues To Fall Short
summary:
Netflix has undertaken efforts over the years to increase its footprint in the world of video games, but it's been a bumpy road, and new data suggests that the company is falling short of its targets.

According to a Netflix memo seen by The Wall Street Journal, only 3.5% of Netflix's subscribers play games monthly. That's 10% behind Netflix's 2026 target for "reach and engagement" for games, the memo said. In 2022, it was reported that fewer than 1% of Netflix subscribers played games on Netflix.

Getting deeper into games is part of Netflix's effort to increase engagement, and it's not the only measure that Netflix has undertaken. The company has also expanded to live sports and podcasts.

Netflix's priorities for gaming have bounced around over the years. At one point in time, Netflix was planning to create AAA games and hired big-name talent. However, Netflix later backtracked, and today the company focuses more on mobile and social games.

Recently, co-CEO Ted Sarandos was asked if Netflix will abandon gaming entirely in the future, and he doesn't think the company will, at least not soon. Sarandos said gaming is appealing to Netflix because, for example, someone who just finished a Netflix show can stay engaged with the brand through Netflix's tie-in games connected to those franchises. Beyond tie-in games for Netflix properties like Stranger Things and Love is Blind, Netflix commissions new games like Unhinged and The Conjuring: Unspoken.

The streaming giant also made a big play in gaming this year by hosting the GTA 6 Extended Look trailer, and it worked to get people to sign up for Netflix and watch on the platform. Netflix previously worked with Take-Two to bring GTA games to the platform. Red Dead Redemption from Take-Two's Rockstar division remains available to play on Netflix.

These new details about Netflix's efforts in gaming come amidst a big shakeup at the company--a number of top executives were let go, or left, earlier this week ahead of Netflix's latest earnings report today, October 20. Netflix's stock price is down 23% this year and 43% over the past 12 months, and investors called on management to make changes to help the stock go back up.

Beyond the executive departures, Netflix laid off 1,000+ people recently, which worked out to about 6% of the company's total workforce; this was the largest round of layoffs in Netflix's history.

title: All Castlevania: Belmont’s Curse Endings Explained
summary:
Those familiar with the Castlevania games know that the series has a history of hiding multiple endings. After all, Symphony of the Night had an entire castle flipped upside down, hidden behind a series of items locked away in hard-to-reach areas. Subsequent games also had entire areas that were only accessible if you equipped certain items at the right time.

Castlevania: Belmont's Curse continues this trend, so if you want to know more about the requirements for unlocking this metroidvania game's best ending, we have the full checklist of things you need to do. On top of that, we'll explain exactly what getting these items unlocks and the potential pitfalls you may encounter on the way to getting any one of the endings.

How many endings are there in Castlevania: Belmont's Curse?

Castlevania: Belmont's Curse has three endings. One is a definitive bad but ultimately false ending that you can encounter during the story. The other two require a little more preparation, with the final ending requiring even more, as well as the use of a specific Tarot card at a crucial moment.

How to get the False Ending

Technically, you can miss this outcome, but it's also part of the story. Keep going through the castle until you reach Death's trap in Dracula's Castle. You can't turn back, but seeing it still gets you to the next part of the game and unlocks a new skin for Rose. You can't get it anywhere else, so it's worth falling for Death's ruse.

This is the simplest of the three to get. Head toward the screen with the Clock Tower, chasing after Isaac and Dracula, and it will begin to warp. Your companions will mostly warn you to turn back before it's too late, but as soon as you enter through one screen, you'll be caught in a loop before Dracula's Chamber. Enter to get the bad ending.

How to get the Normal Ending

Continue playing the game from the False Ending, and make sure you pick up the Shadow Arcana from Notre Dame Cathedral to avoid falling for Death's trick. This also requires that you get the Builder, Occultist, and Artist Arcana to unlock the path to Notre Dame. If you're stuck, you can read the Clock Tower guide for help finding the Builder, the Star Chart guide for assistance with those pesky constellations in the Library, and the Alucard Paintings guide for tips to find the Artist Arcana.

Eventually, you'll face off against both Isaac (a boss at the very tippy top of the Clock Tower) and Dracula just a few screens ahead of him in the Master's Quarters. After two phases, Dracula will begin spreading his curse. Do nothing, and the game will end with the regular ending.

How to get the Good Ending

This one requires you to do a few things first before confronting Dracula at his lair. The first step is to find and complete the four Virtues Trials in Notre Dame Cathedral. These come in the form of stained glass windows in the Room of the Four Virtues toward the top left of the area.

Each one has a challenge that requires you to equip the following Arcana to unlock. This is the order from left to right:

  • Warrior: This needs the Joan of Arc Arcana equipped, which makes you fight a more powerful two-phase rematch against her.
  • Whisperer: This one requires you to find the Miser's three eyes, defeat him, then give the coins you find in Miser's boss room to the Ferryman. This is an obstacle course against a flooding room.
  • Judge: Complete the Judge's Test to get this Arcana. Here you'll fight a big gauntlet of tough foes.
  • Sage: You'll need to beat Succubus in the Hall of Mirrors after breaking all the Sage's Seals, then meet Eleanor of Acquitane in the Tomb of the Noble Queen, which is in the Holy Innocents' Cemetery toward the left side of the entire area. It's close to the shortcut to the Catacombs of Paris. This mirror houses a series of timed challenges where you need to not get hit by buzzsaws.

The next phase is to face off against your doppelganger. Enter the central stained glass window and prepare for battle. With the best weapons and relics equipped and a decent level, you shouldn't have an issue. This will reward you by changing The Curse Arcana into The Self.

Finally, you'll need to completely maximize the newly acquired Arcana card by finishing its Works of Mercy challenges:

  • Kill four enemies with a single cast of this spell five times.
  • Explore 85% of the whole map.
  • Heal back up to full life using this spell ten times.

At its maximum level, it'll be potent enough for you to use after the second phase of the Dracula fight to dispel his curse completely and get the best ending.

On top of that, we'll explain exactly what getting these items unlocks and the potential pitfalls you may encounter on the way to getting any one of the endings.

How many endings are there in Castlevania: Belmont's Curse?

Castlevania: Belmont's Curse has three endings. One is a definitive bad but ultimately false ending that you can encounter during the story. The other two require a little more preparation, with the final ending requiring even more, as well as the use of a specific Tarot card at a crucial moment.

How to get the False Ending

Technically, you can miss this outcome, but it's also part of the story. Keep going through the castle until you reach Death's trap in Dracula's Castle. You can't turn back, but seeing it still gets you to the next part of the game and unlocks a new skin for Rose. You can't get it anywhere else, so it's worth falling for Death's ruse.

This is the simplest of the three to get. Head toward the screen with the Clock Tower, chasing after Isaac and Dracula, and it will begin to warp. Your companions will mostly warn you to turn back before it's too late, but as soon as you enter through one screen, you'll be caught in a loop before Dracula's Chamber. Enter to get the bad ending.

How to get the Normal Ending

Continue playing the game from the False Ending, and make sure you pick up the Shadow Arcana from Notre Dame Cathedral to avoid falling for Death's trick. This also requires that you get the Builder, Occultist, and Artist Arcana to unlock the path to Notre Dame. If you're stuck, you can read the Clock Tower guide for help finding the Builder, the Star Chart guide for assistance with those pesky constellations in the Library, and the Alucard Paintings guide for tips to find the Artist Arcana.

Eventually, you'll face off against both Isaac (a boss at the very tippy top of the Clock Tower) and Dracula just a few screens ahead of him in the Master's Quarters. After two phases, Dracula will begin spreading his curse. Do nothing, and the game will end with the regular ending.

How to get the Good Ending

This one requires you to do a few things first before confronting Dracula at his lair. The first step is to find and complete the four Virtues Trials in Notre Dame Cathedral. These come in the form of stained glass windows in the Room of the Four Virtues toward the top left of the area.

Each one has a challenge that requires you to equip the following Arcana to unlock. This is the order from left to right:

  • Warrior: This needs the Joan of Arc Arcana equipped, which makes you fight a more powerful two-phase rematch against her.
  • Whisperer: This one requires you to find the Miser's three eyes, defeat him, then give the coins you find in Miser's boss room to the Ferryman. This is an obstacle course against a flooding room.
  • Judge: Complete the Judge's Test to get this Arcana. Here you'll fight a big gauntlet of tough foes.
  • Sage: You'll need to beat Succubus in the Hall of Mirrors after breaking all the Sage's Seals, then meet Eleanor of Acquitane in the Tomb of the Noble Queen, which is in the Holy Innocents' Cemetery toward the left side of the entire area. It's close to the shortcut to the Catacombs of Paris. This mirror houses a series of timed challenges where you need to not get hit by buzzsaws.

The next phase is to face off against your doppelganger. Enter the central stained glass window and prepare for battle. With the best weapons and relics equipped and a decent level, you shouldn't have an issue. This will reward you by changing The Curse Arcana into The Self.

Finally, you'll need to completely maximize the newly acquired Arcana card by finishing its Works of Mercy challenges:

  • Kill four enemies with a single cast of this spell five times.
  • Explore 85% of the whole map.
  • Heal back up to full life using this spell ten times.

At its maximum level, it'll be potent enough for you to use after the second phase of the Dracula fight to dispel his curse completely and get the best ending.

title: How To Solve The Star Chart Puzzles In Castlevania: Belmont’s Curse
summary:
As you explore the Library in Castlevania: Belmont's Curse, you may have noticed rings of glyphs you can bounce off, surrounding spheres with one of three designs. These are planetary spheres, each depicting a figure representing the constellation you need to trace with the glyphs to unlock a larger glyph that bounces you high in the sky.

Now, you can hunt for these constellations in the form of clues left behind in the various rooms of the Library. If you're searching for all the weapons, you probably should take that approach. However, if you only want the combos for each one of the three designs so you can see them at a glance, then we have all the answers.

How to solve the Star Chart puzzles

There are three designs that any of these giant Star Charts could represent: Man, Woman, and Skeleton. Each has a specific design to trace on the six stars, and you only need to touch the glyphs in any order to activate it. If you mess up, just land nearby and try again. You can see all three constellations below:

To reach the top and fight The Occultist, you'll need to trace all three designs from the center of the Planetarium, then follow the path to reach the boss door. We won't spoil the boss here, but we highly recommend equipping any Relics that increase your damage with easy trigger conditions, or anything that reduces spell mana costs.
